granite.note: Uncountable: made of granite, a granite floor (not "a granite").
ex: Our new kitchen counters are made of granite.
Granite is a very hard and heavy stone.
The old steps in front of the bank are granite.
Is granite more expensive than wood for a table?

Catholic.note: Most often "Catholic" is an adjective: "a Catholic church." Always write it with a capital C.
ex: Her family are Catholics and go to church every Sunday.
Is he a Catholic or a Protestant?
Many Catholics in this town go to the same church.
My grandmother is a Catholic, and she prays every morning.

antique.note: Often an adjective: "an antique table" (old and valuable).
ex: This old clock is a valuable antique.
My grandmother collects antiques from all over the country.
You can buy antiques at the market on Sundays.
Is this chair a real antique or a copy?

mil.note: Most often "mil" is informal for "million": "ten mil". As a unit, it is 1/1000 of an inch.
ex: Buy plastic sheeting that is at least six mil thick.
These heavy trash bags are three mil thick.
Is this plastic film four mil or six mil?
The paint should be about two mils thick when dry.

derby.note: Also a big horse race, and in the US a round hard hat (a "bowler").

quiz.note: In US schools, a "quiz" is also a short test: "a math quiz."
ex: We go to a quiz night at the bar every Thursday.
Our team won the quiz by two points.
She made a fun quiz for her friend's birthday party.
Do you want to join our team for the quiz?

present.note: Most often "present" means "here" or "now": "All students are present." It is also a verb.

biker.note: Usually a motorcycle rider; in the US sometimes also a person on a bicycle.

cycle.note: As a verb, "cycle" means to ride a bike: "I cycle to work."
ex: The washing machine has a short cycle for light clothes.
The life cycle of a frog has four stages.
Sleep has several cycles every night.
The cycle of the seasons repeats every year.
We watched a scary thriller last night.
This thriller kept me awake until two in the morning.
She writes crime thrillers about a young police officer.
Do you prefer thrillers or comedies on weekends?

ketchup.note: Uncountable: some ketchup, a lot of ketchup (not "a ketchup").

ex: A tall cedar grows in the corner of our yard.
The old wooden chest is made of cedar.
Cedar trees have a fresh and pleasant smell.
They planted a row of cedars along the road.

boost.note: Most often "boost" is a verb: "Coffee boosts my energy."

leasing.note: For one contract, say "a lease": "We signed a two-year lease."
ex: Leasing a car can cost less each month than buying.
The company offers leasing for office equipment.
We chose leasing because we didn't have enough money.
Is leasing a better choice for a small business?

clone.note: Also a verb: "Scientists cloned a sheep."

hype.note: Uncountable: a lot of hype (not "a hype").
ex: There is a lot of hype around the new phone.
The movie was good, but not as good as the hype.
Don't believe all the hype about this diet.
Is the new restaurant worth the hype?

cola.note: In the US, any sweet fizzy drink is often called "soda."
ex: Can I have a cola with ice, please?
He drinks too much cola and not enough water.
We ordered a pizza and two large colas.
This cola is too sweet for me.

prestige.note: Uncountable: a lot of prestige (not "a prestige").
ex: A job at this hospital brings a lot of prestige.
The university has great prestige around the world.
He lost his prestige after the scandal.
For her, money matters more than prestige.

loft.note: In British English, "loft" also means the room under the roof (an attic).

compliance.note: Uncountable. Often "in compliance with": "in compliance with the rules."

recorder.note: Also a simple musical instrument you blow into, like a small flute.

ex: The whole city was in lockdown for two months.
We worked from home during the lockdown.
All schools closed during the first lockdown.
Are shops open during the lockdown?
Psst, come over here and look at this!
Psst, I think your shoe is untied.
Psst, can you pass me a pen, please?
Psst, don't tell anyone about the surprise party.

flyer.note: Also a person who travels by plane: "a frequent flyer."

recycling.note: Uncountable: "put it in the recycling" (not "a recycling").
ex: Our city has a good recycling program for plastic.
Please put the empty bottles in the recycling.
Recycling helps reduce the amount of waste we make.
Which day do they pick up the recycling here?

aspirin.note: Both "an aspirin" (one pill) and "some aspirin" are correct.

graffiti.note: Uncountable: some graffiti, a lot of graffiti (not "a graffiti").
ex: The wall near the station is covered with graffiti.
Some kids painted graffiti on the old bridge.
The city cleans graffiti off buildings every week.
Some people think graffiti is a kind of art.

take.note: Most often "take" is a verb: "Take the bus." "Take a photo."

abdomen.note: Formal; in everyday speech people say "stomach" or "belly".

ex: The soundtrack of this movie is amazing.
I listen to the game soundtrack while I work.
She bought the soundtrack on vinyl.
Who wrote the soundtrack for this film?

replay.note: Also a verb: "They replayed the goal." In US sports TV, often "instant replay."
ex: Let's watch the replay of the goal again.
The replay showed that the ball was out.
You can watch a replay of the game online.
The referee checked the video replay before his decision.

substitute.note: Often a verb: "You can substitute honey for sugar." Also a replacement teacher or player.

messiah.note: In religion, written with a capital: "the Messiah."

anime.note: Usually uncountable: "I watch anime." For one show: "an anime series."

quarantine.note: Usually "in quarantine": "The dog is in quarantine."
ex: The travelers had to stay in quarantine for a week.
Our quarantine lasted fourteen days, and we stayed home.
They put the sick dog in quarantine.
We cooked a lot of new dishes during quarantine.
This retailer sells clothes online and in stores.
The retailer cut prices before the holidays.
Many small retailers closed their stores this year.
Is it better to buy from an official retailer?
